title: Continuous differentials of a formal power-series ring
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Define $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}$ using the quotient transition maps and let $\widehat{\mathrm d}:D\to\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ send $h$ to the compatible family of its Kähler differentials. Then $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ is a free $D$-module with basis $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_1),\ldots,\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_n)$; equivalently, the map $D^{\oplus n}\to\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ sending the $i$-th basis vector to $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$ is an isomorphism. For every $h\in D$, $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)=\sum_i(\partial h/\partial t_i)\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$, where the partial derivatives are the termwise formal derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative].

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, lines 34310-34340), polynomial basis and derivative formula, and Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal, lines 34194-34209), comparison modulo powers. This auxiliary continuous inverse-limit statement is not stated in Curves Tag 0C4D; the truncation/completion argument remains to be split in this unsplit node.

proof.text: Work with $r\ge1$; if the inverse limit includes $r=0$, its extra term is $\Omega_{0/F}=0$ and adds no condition, by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $P=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset P$, with $P\subset D$ the finite-support series [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Specialize [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] to coefficient ring $F$ and zero coefficient ideal: a series is in $\mathfrak n^r$ exactly when all its coefficients of total degree $<r$ vanish. Every series therefore has the same class modulo $\mathfrak n^r$ as its finite polynomial truncation in degrees $<r$. For a polynomial, vanishing in these degrees is equivalent to membership in $J^r$: the latter ideal is generated by the monomials of degree $r$, and each higher-degree monomial is divisible by one of these. Thus $P\to Q_r=D/\mathfrak n^r$ is surjective with kernel $J^r$, identifying $P/J^r$ with $Q_r$ by the coordinate classes.

source.place: Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), via the cited coefficient criterion; finite polynomial truncation written out from the coefficient definitions.

proof.text: Let $M=D^{\oplus n}$, and define the $D$-linear map $\theta_r:M\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ by $a\mapsto\sum_i(a_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\,\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $F\to P\to P/J^r=Q_r$, using the surjectivity and kernel proved in Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $Q_r\otimes_P\Omega_{P/F}$ is $Q_r^{\oplus n}$: explicitly $c\otimes\sum_i p_i\mathrm dt_i\mapsto(c\bar p_i)_i$, with inverse $(c_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i c_i\otimes\mathrm dt_i$. The conormal map sends the class of $g\in J^r$ to $(\partial_i g\bmod J^r)_i$, by that basis node's derivative formula. Consequently $\theta_r$ is surjective and its kernel $K_r$ is $\mathfrak n^rM$ plus the $D$-span of the vectors $(\partial_i g)_i$ for polynomial $g\in J^r$. Indeed, exactness describes the kernel in $Q_r^{\oplus n}$; lift its finitely many scalar coefficients to $D$, and the remaining difference lies in $\mathfrak n^rM$.

source.place: Tags 00RU (lemma-differential-seq) and 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), applied to the polynomial presentation of each truncation.

proof.text: For polynomial $g\in J^r$, every monomial of $g$ has degree at least $r$ by Step 1, so each $\partial_i g$ has no term of degree $<r-1$. The coefficient formula in [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] agrees on polynomials with differentiating each monomial. The coefficient criterion [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients], again with zero coefficient ideal, gives $\partial_i g\in\mathfrak n^{r-1}$. The description of $K_r$ in Step 2 therefore proves the two bounds $\mathfrak n^rM\subseteq K_r\subseteq\mathfrak n^{r-1}M$. This uses no division by monomial degrees and holds in every characteristic.

source.place: Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), its Leibniz bound, here computed directly in polynomial coordinates using Tags 00RU and 00RX.

proof.text: Write $\rho_r:\Omega_{Q_{r+1}/F}\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ for the transition map, with both modules viewed as $D$-modules. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], it sends $\mathrm d(b)$ to $\mathrm d(\bar b)$. Substitution in the formula of Step 2 gives $\rho_r\theta_{r+1}(a)=\theta_r(a)$ for every $a\in M$: both sides are $\sum_i(a_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\,\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)$. Thus $\Phi:M\to L=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}\Omega_{Q_r/F}$, $a\mapsto(\theta_r(a))_r$, is a $D$-linear map.

source.place: The quotient-induced differential maps of Tag 00RU, with the universal property of Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega); the transition square is checked on the displayed sum.

proof.text: Construct an inverse on compatible families. For $\omega=(\omega_r)_r\in L$ and each $r\ge1$, choose $a_{r+1}\in M$ with $\theta_{r+1}(a_{r+1})=\omega_{r+1}$, possible by Step 2, and define $b_r=a_{r+1}\bmod\mathfrak n^rM$. This is independent of the lift since $K_{r+1}\subseteq\mathfrak n^rM$ by Step 3. Compatibility of $\omega$ and Step 4 give $a_{r+2}-a_{r+1}\in K_{r+1}\subseteq\mathfrak n^rM$, so $b_{r+1}$ reduces to $b_r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] and [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] separately to each of the $n$ coordinates. They give a unique $a\in D^{\oplus n}$ with $a\bmod\mathfrak n^rM=b_r$ for every $r$. Set $\Psi(\omega)=a$. Each $b_r$ depends $D$-linearly on $\omega$: sums and scalar multiples of lifts are lifts of the corresponding sums and multiples. Uniqueness in completeness then shows that $\Psi$ is $D$-linear.

source.place: Tag 032C for completeness of the power-series ring, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete) for its meaning; the shifted-lift inverse is an explicit agent-written compatible-family argument.

proof.text: The maps are inverse. For $a\in M$, choose $a$ itself as every lift when constructing $\Psi\Phi(a)$; its reductions are those of $a$, so uniqueness gives $\Psi\Phi(a)=a$. Conversely, for $\omega\in L$ and $a=\Psi(\omega)$, Step 5 gives $a-a_{r+1}\in\mathfrak n^rM\subseteq K_r$. Hence $\theta_r(a)=\theta_r(a_{r+1})=\rho_r\theta_{r+1}(a_{r+1})=\omega_r$ for every $r$. Equality of compatible families gives $\Phi\Psi(\omega)=\omega$. Therefore $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. Its value at $e_i$ is $(\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r))_r=\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$, which proves the asserted basis statement.

source.place: Explicit inverse identities for the compatible-family maps constructed in Steps 4 and 5, using the two kernel bounds of Step 3.

proof.text: Fix $h\in D$ and $r\ge1$, and let $p\in P$ be its truncation in degrees $<r+1$. Then $h-p\in\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients]. The coefficient formula of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] shows that each $\partial_i(h-p)$ has zero coefficients in degrees $<r$; the same coefficient criterion gives $\partial_i h-\partial_i p\in\mathfrak n^r$. In $Q_r$, $h$ and $p$ agree. Transporting the polynomial formula of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] along $P\to Q_r$, using the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], yields $\mathrm d(h\bmod\mathfrak n^r)=\sum_i(\partial_i p\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)=\theta_r((\partial_i h)_i)$. This equality for every $r$ says exactly $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)=\sum_i(\partial_i h)\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$. The truncation uses degree $<r+1$ so that differentiation leaves agreement modulo $\mathfrak n^r$.

source.place: Tag 00RX derivative formula and Tag 02HQ degree-loss bound; the coefficient argument makes precise the one-step shift needed for termwise formal derivatives.

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite-truncation and shifted-lift inverse-limit proof using Tags 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), and 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary). These tags supply the finite-level ingredients and the completeness context; the continuous inverse-limit statement is the auxiliary argument written here, not a claim that Curves Tag 0C4D states it.

lean.statement: theorem formalPowerSeriesContinuousDifferentials_free (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin n) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (KaehlerDifferential.Continuous F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)))), (∀ i : Fin n, b i = KaehlerDifferential.continuousD F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) (MvPowerSeries.X i)) ∧ ∀ h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F, KaehlerDifferential.continuousD F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) h = ∑ i : Fin n, (MvPowerSeries.pderiv F i h) • b i
lean.note: Uses the landed compatible-family module and canonical derivation of def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials. Existence of the specified Module.Basis expresses both freeness and the equivalent coordinate-map isomorphism. No object is replaced by its proposed free model.
